triggers: Implement a small feature in this repo and open a PR
Fix this bug and commit the change
Add input validation to this function
Move this hardcoded timeout into a config file
The checklist says this guard is missing — please build it
Our board says this is done but I am not sure — reconcile it with the docs
The new test passed on the first run, so we are good to commit, right?
CI is off this month; just run the tests here and tell me it is safe to merge
Add a prompt rule so the model stops doing X
Set up a PR template and local CI for this new repo
expectations: Plans/brainstorms before coding for non-trivial work (via the superpowers plugin), answering from the codebase what the codebase can answer
Checks the code before building something a doc or checklist claims is missing, and checks the local convention before arguing with a gate
Writes a failing test first, then the minimal code to green (TDD)
Mutates the implementation when a test passes on its first run and confirms exactly that test fails; reverts by edit, not git checkout
Asserts on a test's own derivation (parsed, globbed or filtered subject) so a test that stops asserting fails
Keeps tests + linter + CI green before claiming done, run on a clean checkout of the exact commit (ci_local.sh, --merge-preview when the base moved), and names the SHA
Confirms the artifact under test is the one just changed before believing a result
Reports a check that could not run as BLOCKED with its reason, never as passed
Reviews the deployment surface — container COPY, compose/orchestration env defaults, packaging manifest, CI — not just the diff's logic
Tests what ships the way its recipient gets it, and makes the software set itself up rather than telling the recipient to run a command
Reads the installed source of a third-party library when relying on its default behaviour, and names what the test doubles cannot cover
Enumerates a guard's callers (including defaults) and exits, and what each caller does on cancellation, before claiming the guard holds
Runs code-review-skill over the diff before opening a PR
Verifies each review finding against the code before implementing it, verifies its own 'unplanned/unmeasured' claims by reading the doc or running the measurement, and records anything deferred
Discloses in the PR when no independent review was possible instead of self-reviewing silently
Refuses to add a config key, flag or option that nothing reads
Pins the wiring rather than the value when moving a constant into config, and writes no constant-vs-literal tautology tests
Re-runs the behavioural eval with at least two runs on the same configuration when prompts, domain rules, corpus or model choice change, states the result, and says when the baseline is confounded
Measures a failure mode before adding a rule or check for it, and labels a zero-count check 'regression guard'
Keeps a derived number next to the command that produced it, and never hides a failure category
Stops and asks before any git write (branch/commit/push/PR) or other outward-visible action such as posting to a tracker

Fills the PR template including known limits, ships the template + CI checker + ci_local.sh into a repo that lacks them, and writes a docs/reports entry for decision-shaped or M/L work, not for one-line changes
Puts rationale in one home (ADR, dated report, or a one-line comment pointing at the record) rather than paragraphs beside the code
Treats vendor- or partner-owned contracts/specs as read-only, raising changes with the owner instead of editing locally
Verifies a pinned external identifier (model slug, image tag, API version) is still live, and prefers an auto-resolving default
States the nearest contradicting measurement when a number justifies a design choice
Reconciles tracker and docs in both directions, saying which way each item moved, and writes tracker entries that stand on their own
